errores.descripcion: Confunde un detalle con la idea principal o toma un dato de otra parte del texto
errores.recomendacion: Ubica la palabra clave de la pregunta en el texto y lee la oración completa antes de elegir.

errores.descripcion: Agrega información que el texto no dice
errores.recomendacion: Elige solo lo que el texto afirma o permite deducir; descarta lo que suena lógico pero no aparece.

errores.descripcion: No reconoce el tipo de texto o su destinatario
errores.recomendacion: Fíjate en el formato (saludo, firma, secciones), el registro y el propósito del texto.

errores.descripcion: Interpreta de forma literal una expresión idiomática o figurada
errores.recomendacion: Si la lectura literal no tiene sentido en el contexto, busca el significado figurado.

errores.descripcion: Hace una inferencia que el texto no sostiene o que lo contradice
errores.recomendacion: Una inferencia válida se apoya en datos del texto; verifica que no contradiga ninguna oración.

errores.descripcion: Elige un significado de la palabra que no corresponde al contexto
errores.recomendacion: Relee la oración y las vecinas: sustituye la palabra por la opción y comprueba que el sentido se mantenga.

errores.descripcion: Confunde la estructura o el propósito del texto (hecho/opinión, causa-efecto, problema-solución, argumentos)
errores.recomendacion: Busca conectores clave: because, as a result (causa-efecto); however, on the other hand (contraste); should, must (persuasión).

errores.descripcion: Elige un título o subtítulo demasiado estrecho, amplio o ajeno al contenido
errores.recomendacion: El título debe abarcar todo el texto o párrafo, no un detalle.

errores.descripcion: Usa un tiempo verbal que no concuerda con el momento o la secuencia de las acciones
errores.recomendacion: Identifica marcadores temporales (yesterday, since, while, if) y el tiempo que exigen.

errores.descripcion: Usa mal la forma del verbo o del adjetivo (gerundio, infinitivo, participio, -ed/-ing)
errores.recomendacion: Después de preposición: -ing; propósito: to + verbo; pasiva: be + participio; sentimientos: -ed.

errores.descripcion: Elige un conector con una relación lógica equivocada
errores.recomendacion: Contraste: however, although. Causa: because. Consecuencia: therefore, so. Tiempo: when, as soon as.

errores.descripcion: La paráfrasis o síntesis cambia el sentido original
errores.recomendacion: Una paráfrasis cambia las palabras pero conserva los hechos y su relación.

errores.descripcion: Usa un registro o tono que no corresponde a la situación
errores.recomendacion: Formal para reportes y desconocidos; informal para amigos. Distingue hechos de opiniones.

errores.descripcion: Usa mal los pronombres relativos
errores.recomendacion: Who: personas. Which: cosas. Where: lugares. No repitas el sujeto después del relativo.

errores.descripcion: Elige una preposición equivocada o calcada del español
errores.recomendacion: Memoriza combinaciones: focus on, for + duración, since + inicio, to + verbo (propósito).

errores.descripcion: No hace concordar el verbo con el núcleo del sujeto
errores.recomendacion: Identifica el núcleo: «the number of students» es singular; «questionnaires» es plural.

errores.descripcion: Forma mal el comparativo o el superlativo
errores.recomendacion: Corto: -er/-est. Largo: more/most. Irregular: good-better-best.

errores.descripcion: Usa mal los artículos
errores.recomendacion: The: referente identificado. A/an: uno cualquiera (según el sonido inicial).

errores.descripcion: Se deja llevar por un falso cognado del español
errores.recomendacion: Actually = en realidad; attend = asistir; assist = ayudar; currently = actualmente.

errores.descripcion: Combina palabras que en inglés no van juntas (calco del español)
errores.recomendacion: Do research, make a mistake, pay attention, take a photo.

errores.descripcion: Confunde lenguaje concreto y abstracto
errores.recomendacion: Concreto: se percibe con los sentidos. Abstracto: ideas, cualidades, emociones.

errores.descripcion: Usa un cuantificador que no concuerda con el sustantivo
errores.recomendacion: Much/little con incontables; many/few con contables.

textos.titulo: Central Library: New Opening Hours and Services
parrafos: From Monday, 2 March, the Central Library will open earlier and close later during the exam period. The new hours are 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, and 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. on Saturdays. The library will remain closed on Sundays and public holidays.

Students can now reserve one of our twelve group study rooms online. Each reservation lasts a maximum of two hours, and rooms must be booked at least one day in advance. Groups must have between three and six members.

Please remember that food is not allowed in any part of the building. Drinks are permitted only in closed bottles. Mobile phones must be on silent mode in the reading rooms on the second and third floors.

If you need help finding information for your research, our librarians offer free 30-minute appointments. You can book one at the information desk on the ground floor or by email at help@centrallibrary.edu.

textos.titulo: Volunteers Wanted at Happy Paws Shelter
parrafos: Do you love animals? Happy Paws Shelter is looking for volunteers to help us care for more than 80 dogs and cats that are waiting for a new home.

Volunteers walk the dogs, clean the cages, feed the animals and help at our adoption events. No experience is necessary, as we provide a free two-hour training session on the first Saturday of every month.
Requirements: you must be at least 17 years old (volunteers aged 15 or 16 may join if they come with a parent), and you must be able to give us at least four hours a week for three months.

Volunteers receive a certificate of social service hours, a Happy Paws T-shirt and, above all, the chance to make a real difference. To apply, fill in the form on our website before 30 April. Places are limited!
Dear students,

I am writing to let you know about two changes to the final project for Introduction to Biology. First, the deadline has been moved from 15 May to 22 May, because the laboratory will be closed for repairs during the second week of May. Second, you may now work in pairs instead of individually; however, each pair must submit only one report, and both names must appear on the first page.
The report should be between 1,500 and 2,000 words and must include at least five academic sources. Reports that are shorter than 1,500 words will lose ten points.
Please send me your partner's name by Friday so that I can organise the presentation schedule. If you prefer to work alone, that is still possible; just let me know.
Best regards, Dr. Laura Méndez

textos.titulo: A Day in the Old Town of San Lázaro
parrafos: The old town of San Lázaro is small enough to explore on foot in one day. Most visitors start at the main square, where the cathedral and the town hall face each other. The cathedral is open to visitors from 9:00 to 13:00 and from 16:00 to 19:00; entrance is free, but photographs are not allowed inside.

Two streets east of the square, the Municipal Market sells fresh fruit, local cheese and traditional sweets. It is busiest on Sunday mornings, when farmers from nearby villages bring their products. If you want to avoid the crowds, go on a weekday.
For the best view of the town, climb the 300 steps to the Chapel of the Hill. The walk takes about 25 minutes and there is little shade, so take water and a hat, especially in summer.
Getting there: buses leave the capital every hour from the North Terminal. The journey takes two and a half hours. There is no train station in San Lázaro.

Many university students believe that staying up all night is the best way to prepare for an exam. Research suggests the opposite. During sleep, the brain does not simply rest; it organises and stores the information we have learned during the day.

In one study, two groups of students learned a list of words in the evening. The first group slept normally, while the second group stayed awake. The next morning, the students who had slept remembered about 20% more words than those who had not.

Lack of sleep also affects attention. When we are tired, it is harder to concentrate, and we make more mistakes in tasks that require careful reading or calculation. As a result, a student who studies all night may know more facts at 3 a.m. but perform worse at 9 a.m.

Experts recommend that young adults sleep between seven and nine hours a night. Reviewing notes for a short time before going to bed and then sleeping well appears to be a far more effective strategy than cramming until dawn.

Every morning, hundreds of cars enter our campus, fill the air with smoke and turn the main avenue into a dangerous place for anyone on foot. It is time for the university to take a bold step: close the campus to private cars.

Some will say that this idea is unrealistic, because many students and teachers live far away. But a car-free campus does not mean a campus that is hard to reach. Cars could be left in a large car park at the entrance, and free electric buses could take people to every faculty in less than ten minutes.

The benefits would be enormous. The air would be cleaner, the noise would drop, and the space now used for parking could become gardens, sports areas and places to study outdoors. Other universities that have tried this have seen more students walking and cycling.
Change is never easy, but we cannot keep putting the health of our community on the back burner. If we want a greener university, we must stop talking and start acting.

textos.titulo: How Puerto Claro Cleaned Its Beaches
parrafos: Ten years ago, the beaches of Puerto Claro were covered with plastic bottles. Tourists stopped coming, fishermen found plastic in their nets, and the city spent a large part of its budget on cleaning.

In 2018, the city council introduced a simple deposit system. Every time people buy a drink in a plastic bottle, they pay a small extra amount. When they return the empty bottle to a machine in a supermarket, they get that money back.

At first, many shop owners complained that the machines took up too much space. However, the results soon convinced them. Within three years, nine out of ten bottles were being returned, and the amount of plastic on the beaches fell dramatically.
Today, Puerto Claro's system is being copied by other coastal towns. Its success shows that people are willing to change their habits when there is a clear and immediate reward.

The axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum) is a salamander found in the wild only in the canals and lakes of Xochimilco, in the south of Mexico City. Unlike most amphibians, it usually keeps its larval features throughout its life: it lives permanently in water and breathes through the feathery gills on the sides of its head.

Axolotls are famous among scientists for their remarkable ability to regenerate. If one loses a leg, it can grow a complete new one, including bones, muscles and nerves. Researchers hope that understanding this process may one day help medicine repair human tissues.

Sadly, the wild population has fallen sharply in recent decades. Water pollution, the growth of the city and the introduction of foreign fish such as carp and tilapia, which eat axolotl eggs and young, have pushed the species to the edge of extinction.

Local farmers and scientists are working together to create "refuges": protected canals where the water is filtered and foreign fish are kept out. You can support this work by visiting the refuges with authorised guides.

Since 2020, many universities have offered courses online, and the debate about which format is better has not stopped. Supporters of online learning point out that it saves time and money: students do not have to travel, and they can watch recorded lessons whenever it suits them.
Online courses can also open the door to people who would otherwise be left out, such as those who work full-time or live in rural areas far from a university.

On the other hand, critics argue that something important is lost when classes take place on a screen. Students have fewer chances to ask spontaneous questions, work in teams or build friendships, and many find it harder to stay motivated without a fixed timetable.

Perhaps the answer is not to choose one side. Many institutions now combine both formats: lectures are recorded and placed online, while class time is used for discussion, laboratory work and group projects.
